items.title: New jobs compute will soon default to Auto access mode for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
items.text: Starting in December 2026, new jobs compute created in the UI will default to Auto access mode in workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Auto uses Standard access mode unless a machine learning runtime, a GPU instance type, or a Databricks Runtime version lower than 14.3 is selected. A cluster policy that enforces a different access mode still takes precedence. Existing jobs are not changed. See Use standard access mode.

items.title: New jobs compute defaults to Auto access mode
items.text: When you create new jobs compute in the UI, the access mode now defaults to Auto instead of Dedicated. Auto uses Standard access mode unless a machine learning runtime, a GPU instance type, or a Databricks Runtime version lower than 14.3 is selected. A cluster policy that enforces a different access mode still takes precedence. Existing jobs are not changed. For workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled, this change takes effect in December 2026. See What's coming. See Use standard access mode.

items.title: Unity Catalog wikis are in Beta
items.text: Unity Catalog wikis are in Beta. A wiki lets your team document a table's meaning, intended use, and sources, then collaborate on that information. Data owners and stewards draft and publish wikis in Catalog Explorer, manually or with Genie Code, and anyone who can view the table's metadata can comment on, suggest edits to, and react to published wikis. Account admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page.

items.id: November_02_2026#Feature: Lakehouse supports the following remote catalog providers for cross-cloud data access.
items.title: Lakehouse supports the following remote catalog providers for cross-cloud data access (GA)
items.text: Lakehouse supports the following remote catalog providers for cross-cloud data access. This feature is generally available (GA). Databricks Unity Catalog on Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud AWS Glue Data Catalog on AWS Snowflake Horizon Catalog on AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Workday Data Lake on AWS or Google Cloud This feature lets you configure federated catalog endpoints to synchronize catalog metadata and query Apache Iceberg tables in remote catalogs directly from Google Cloud using BigQuery, Managed Service for Apache Spark, and Apache Spark without migrating data or building complex ETL pipelines. You can route background metadata refresh and queries over the public internet or privately over Cross-Cloud Interconnect, and protect cross-cloud data access with VPC Service Controls service perimeters. items.id: November_02_2026#Feature: You can now use BigQuery change history and continuous queries for Apache Iceberg managed tables in Lakehouse.
items.title: You can now use BigQuery change history and continuous queries for Apache Iceberg managed tables in Lakehouse (GA)
items.text: You can now use BigQuery change history and continuous queries for Apache Iceberg managed tables in Lakehouse. You can use the APPENDS table-valued function (TVF) to track rows appended to Apache Iceberg managed tables over a specified time range, and use BigQuery continuous queries to read incoming data from and write output rows to Apache Iceberg managed tables. This feature is generally available (GA). For more information, see Work with change history and Introduction to continuous queries.
